newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan discussing Mirage fighter deal with France.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan discussing Mirage fighter deal with France.

text.p: A Pakistan Air Force (PAF) team is in France discussing the planned purchase of 32 Mirage 2000-5 fighters, PAF chief Air Chief Marshal Abbas Khattak said on Monday.

He told reporters that Pakistan had asked France to transfer technology with the top-of-the-range jets, seen as an alternative to U.S. F-16s whose sale was blocked by Washignton in 1990 owing to suspicions over Pakistan's nuclear programme.
"We wanted 85 percent of the airplane's frame and 50 percent of avionics (instruments) to be produced in Pakistan," Khattak said.
That production would be in collaboration with the United Arab Emirates and Turkey, he added.
France initially agreed to that proposal but later insisted on signing the agreement only for the sale 32 Mirage 2000-5s, Khattak said.
He said the PAF team now in France was still working out details about various aspects of the purchase.

Khattak said France had asked for $47 million apiece for the aircraft but Pakistan could get them for much less if their avionic instruments, which alone would cost $27 million per plane, were changed for another system.
"We can have a system (of avionics) closer to five to six million dollars if we want to buy those airplanes," he said.
Khattak said Pakistan had no option but to buy costly Mirages after failing to get Russian SU-27s.
He said Pakistan needed high-tech planes to increase its defence capability against arch-rival India, which he said was investing huge amounts of money in upgrading its air force.
The United States halted military sales to Pakistan in 1990 under its so-called Pressler Amendment law because of Islamabad's alleged programme to build nuclear weapons.
However, Washington eased the sanctions last year when Congress approved delivery of some blocked military equipment, but not the F-16s, some of which Pakistan had paid for.
